sentences.text: Mr. Apoorv Joshi - Advocate for the appellants.

Mr. Jai Gopal Chouksey appearing on behalf of
Advocate General[r- 1].

Heard on IA No.2914/2026, an application filed under Section 430 of BNSS for grant of temporary suspension of sentence of the appellant No.2 Rameshwar, who has been convicted under sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of the IPC and sentenced to undergo 5 years R.I., 5 years R.I., 5 years R.I., 2 years R.I., and 5 years with fine of Rs.2,000/-, Rs.2,000/-, Rs.2,000/- , Rs.2,000/- and Rs.2,000/- with default stipulation vide order dated 23.12.2025 in ST No.18/2021 by the ASJ,
Jawad, District Neemuch (M.P.).
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.
It is further submitted that appellant no.2 Rameshwar is not keeping good health inside jail.
As per medical documents procured under RTI, the appellant has been suffering from left chest pain with cough from quite some time.
Even the ECG report available on record shows some irregularities.
Prolonged chest pain could be a sign of some serious underlying illness like pneumonia or even cardiac issues.
Hence prayed for suspension of sentence and release of the appellant on bail.
Counsel for State has opposed the application of suspension.

Considering the ailment of the appellant No.2, without expressing any opinion on the merits, (IA No.2914/2026) is hereby allowed and it is directed that execution of jail sentence passed against the appellant No.2 Rameshwar shall remain suspended temporarily for a period of 02 months from the date of his release subject to his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court.
The appellant No.2 shall immediately surrender after expiry of period of 02 months from the date of his release.
In case of non-surrender, the learned trial Court shall be free to take any coercive action against the appellant No.2 to ensure his surrender before the trial Court.
List for final hearing in due course.
